Subject: Model fit + evals follow-up — JSON schema & tool-calling

Jamie — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our side so we can scope an eval run: 

Summary of your requirements (as I understood them):
- Structured transaction enrichment where the model returns a strict JSON object per transaction (fields: merchant_category, merchant_normalized, risk_flags, enrichment_tags[], confidence_score)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for single-turn enrichment; throughput ~1k requests/day initially, bursty peaks up to 5k/day
- Strong JSON schema compliance is required (customers will validate via automated parsers)
- Need reproducible evals using your sample dataset and our prompt sets; want clear metrics for schema compliance and fidelity/regression tracking

Initial recommended models to evaluate: 
- Redwood-serve-1 (our tool-calling optimized variant; good tradeoff for structured output and low latency)
- Llama-3-13b-quant (open model baseline we can run under similar runtime configs)

I’ve attached: prompt_set_v1.csv (initial prompt templates) and initial_benchmark_summary.pdf (high-level results from our internal tests). I also uploaded a folder with the prompt sets + eval harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/folder/0AExampleBenchmarkLink

Questions / next steps: 
1) Can you provide a small sample of your production payloads (synthetic/anonymized is fine) — that lets us run the exact JSON schema validation and measure real-world compliance. If easier you can upload to s3://fintechco-samples/sample_transactions.json or send as an attachment.
2) Assuming we have the sample data, we’ll run a 3-day eval comparing Redwood-serve-1 vs the Llama baseline with the prompt set and report: schema compliance, parseable JSON rate, token cost, latency p50/p95, and a small human quality check on a 200-sample subset.
3) Would you like us to include an A/B where we try a constrained-decoding approach (output-only-JSON + low-temp) vs a parsing-retry strategy? We typically find constrained-decoding + schema-enforced parsing yields the best compliance for production.

I’ll loop in Neha (SE) and Rishi (infra) on the technical approach — they’ll propose concrete decoder settings and retry logic. Let me know if the above matches your expectations and we’ll schedule a 30-minute sync to kick off the eval.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Thanks for the sample, Jamie — this is perfect. Quick notes from our side and what we’ll run in the eval: 

How we measure schema compliance (short):
- We use a strict JSON Schema checker (explicit field names, types, required fields). Each model output is validated against the schema; metrics reported: parseable_rate (valid JSON parse), schema_compliance_rate (passes schema validator), and field_accuracy (for fields where we have ground truth).

Initial internal baseline (from running your prompt_set_v1 on a 500-sample subset):
- Redwood-serve-1: parseable_rate 94%, schema_compliance_rate 92%, median latency 160ms, p95 280ms
- Llama-3-13b-quant baseline: parseable_rate 86%, schema_compliance_rate 83%, median latency 240ms, p95 410ms

What we’ll include in the eval report:
- Full compliance breakdown by field (merchant_category, merchant_normalized, risk_flags, enrichment_tags[], confidence_score)
- Token cost and latency distribution (p50/p95/p99)
- A small human review (200 samples) for quality regressions vs the current rule-based outputs you’re using

Proposed decoder/settings experiments: 
A) Constrained generation (force JSON-only output using system prompts + output parsers) — Temp=0.0, max_tokens tuned per prompt
B) Relaxed generation + parse-and-retry (allow free text but if parser fails, retry up to 2 times with stricter prompt) — Temp=0.2
C) Tool/function-calling mode (function signature enforces shape and our SDK validates before returning to caller)

I attached recommended_prompt_set_v2.csv and prelim eval results (eval_results_20260322.csv) with the above experiments summarized. Neha / Rishi — can you add any infra / SDK notes for the JSON enforcement & retry strategy?

Next steps: 
1) We’ll run the full 2k-sample eval and share a detailed report by Wed 3/25.
2) Schedule 30-min sync next Tue/Wed to review results and discuss rollout options.
3) If the eval looks good, we’ll produce an integration checklist and a small pilot (1-2 weeks) to validate at scale.

Thanks — looping Neha and Rishi in.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: RE: Model fit + evals follow-up — JSON schema & tool-calling

Hi Jamie — quick technical notes / recommended implementation for best JSON schema compliance when doing tool/function calling: 

1) Prompt + decoder settings we recommend for production JSON outputs:
- System: "You are a JSON-only generator. Output must be a single JSON object matching the provided schema. Do not include any explanatory text."
- Temperature: 0.0 for deterministic outputs; if you need diversity set to 0.1
- Top-p: 0.9; max_tokens: adjusted per record size
- Use our function_call feature with an explicit signature that mirrors the schema. This allows the runtime to return structured objects that map directly to the SDK types.

2) Validation + retry strategy (practical):
- Step 1: Parse output. If parse succeeds and schema validator passes -> accept
- Step 2: If parse fails or schema fails -> retry up to 2 times with an augmented prompt: "Return only valid JSON matching the schema. If you cannot, return an empty object {} and an error_code." Also reduce temperature to 0.0 on retries.
- Step 3: If still invalid -> fallback to a deterministic rule-based enrichment and tag as "fallback_rule" in the response for auditability.

3) Confidence scores: we can return per-field confidence estimates using the model's token-level logit probabilities aggregated heuristically. For stricter guarantees, include a human-in-the-loop flag on low-confidence records (confidence_score < 0.6).

4) SDK support & infra considerations:
- The Redwood SDK includes a JSON schema validator hook you can enable client-side to surface parse failures immediately.
- For high-throughput, enable batching with prefix caching for repeated merchant names to reduce token cost. We’ll include batching guidance in the report.

I’ll drop a short example function signature in the shared Drive folder and link to our docs: https://redwood.inference/docs/tool-calling-json-schema

If you want, Rishi and I can run a short sandbox integration call with your infra team to walk through S3 access and API keys.

—Neha
